text:
rachel kim: quick sync — i've been sketching a 'delegate' model for rollout decisions. idea: router makes fast, best-effort choices using a tiny local rule set + cache. a separate policy service (stateful) owns the hard decisions, long-term scoring, credits, and audit.

tom vasquez: sounds promising. main win is keeping p99 low on the hot path. what's the local rule set look like?

rachel kim: local =: tenant baseline mapping, emergency hard-fail rules (e.g., model down), and short-lived overrides from the policy service (ttl). If policy unreachable, router falls back to baseline or last-known override.

li wei: important: how do we handle canary crediting across tenants? single global pool will create noisy neighbors. suggest per-tenant budget + optional shared overflow pool.

rachel kim: agree. model: tenant_credit{allocated, spent, decay_window}. policy debits credits when it routes canary traffic; if tenant out of credits, policy returns the safe variant.

nina rodriguez: what about measuring impact? policy should emit a delta event when it moves weight > X% or when safety_score crosses threshold. we can drive alerts and automated throttles.

li wei: also propose mirror probes: for early detection, mirror 5-10% of requests to canary variant asynchronously and compare responses. probe results feed into the safety score, but mirror must be rate-limited per-tenant.

tom vasquez: router implementation detail: don't block on policy. flow: 1) check local cache; 2) if stale, return cached decision & async-refresh; 3) if `force_live=true` (rare), block with short timeout.

rachel kim: nice. `force_live` used for admin tests only. default path must be sub-50ms.

li wei: decision payload sketch (keeps it minimal):
```
Decision {
  variant: string;        // variant id to route to
  weight: float;         // suggested traffic weight (0..1)
  ttl_ms: int;           // how long router can cache
  epoch: int;            // decision version for invalidate
  advice: enum {LOCAL_ONLY, ALLOW_MIRROR, FORCE_PROBE} ;
  safety_score: float;   // 0..1 low->high risk
  reason: string;
}
```

nina rodriguez: +audit fields: `credit_consumed: int` and `policy_id` so we can trace who made the call. auditors will ask.

tom vasquez: rollback semantics? prefer automated soft rollback: policy reduces weight in steps, router smooths transitions over `smooth_window_ms`. hard rollback allowed if safety_score > 0.9 or manual.

li wei: smoothing constraints: router should expose a small API to accept weight deltas and apply them by steps: `step_ms` and `max_step_pct`. example: `step_ms=500, max_step_pct=0.05` -> move at most 5% every 500ms.
rachel kim: failure modes: if policy consistently unreachable for N seconds, route to tenant baseline and emit an incident. define N=10s for interactive, longer for batch.

nina rodriguez: telemetry: policy emits a decision event stream with fields {tenant, model, policy_id, decision, safety_score, credit_change}. our observability team will create dashboards and alert rules.

li wei: security: policy service must validate caller identity (router instance id) and sign decision blobs so router can detect tampering. lightweight HMAC ok.
tom vasquez: test plan: 1) local router-only mode (no policy) to validate smoothing and baseline, 2) policy in staging with canned safety_score scenarios, 3) long-run soak with tenant overflow enabled.

rachel kim: perf note: policy must support batched queries. router should attach aggregated stats rather than every single request: e.g., `stats{p50,p95,error_rate}` per window. policy returns decision keyed to the aggregated key.

nina rodriguez: ops-runbook highlights to write: how to promote policy decisions, emergency manual override, interpreting safety_score, audit chase for credit depletion, and how to handle signature mismatches.

li wei: tiny proto addition: `Decision.epoch` plus `Decision.signature` so routers can detect stale/corrupt payloads and refuse to apply.

rachel kim: timeline: i'll draft RFC follow-up with the proto sketches and runbook outline by Friday. spike: we'll add TTL cache + smoothing to a router dev branch to validate no regressions.

tom vasquez: thumbs up. one last ask: include a simple CLI to burn credits in staging so product teams can exercise canaries without affecting real tenants.
